name: Claudia A. Nasraty
headline: I Turn Moving Parts Into Forward Motion
tagline: Over 17 years of experience spanning project management, program management, and business operations, with a consistent focus on cross-functional coordination, stakeholder management, and helping people work better together.
summary:
My approach to work was shaped before I had the language for it. Early in my career I joined a telecommunications company in Kabul, Afghanistan, an international, fast-moving, multicultural environment where I quickly learned that getting work done is never just about tasks and timelines. It is about listening first, earning trust, and understanding how people actually work together. That experience set the foundation for everything that followed.

Over the past 17 years, across project management, program management, and business operations, I have walked into complex situations, figured out what the work actually needs, built the structure to support it, and made sure the people doing the work felt supported while it happened. Most recently, I joined ContextualY as employee number one, where I built the operational foundation for a newly launched B2B insights firm from the ground up. There were no existing systems, just a blank page and a team that needed to hit the ground running.

I think about operations as the thing that makes good work possible. Not more process for the sake of it, but the kind of clarity, structure, and follow-through that removes friction so people can focus on what they are actually there to do. I care just as much about the people side of this as the operational side. The best environments I have been part of are the ones where people communicate openly, support each other, and make it genuinely easier to move forward together. That is what I am always working toward, whether or not it is in my job description.

I also pay close attention to how AI tools can improve the way work actually gets done. Not as a trend to keep up with, but as a practical question I bring to my own workflow first: does this actually help, and does it hold up when the work gets real?

The rest of my life is just as important to me, and honestly it shapes the professional I am more than I can fully explain. I am a wife, a mom to a 7-year-old who keeps me very honest, and an active member of my community. I am also a passionate home baker, and baking may seem far from operations, but to me they are more connected than they look. Both are about structure, precision, and repeatability. Not hoping for a good result, but creating the conditions for one. That connection might say more about how I work than anything else on this page.
